new_statements.rule_in_words: Gungbe is described as a tone language (two underlying tones H and L across Eastern Gbe per Gbeto 2004, whose comparison tables include Gun forms); no open source states where word stress falls or says explicitly that stress is absent or non-contrastive. The only 'stress' in the Gbe phonological literature we could see is Capo 1991 p. 22 on English loanwords whose stressed final syllable receives a falling tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: not mentioned in any opened source
new_statements.domain_note: The tonal statement is a one-line footnote in a syntax paper by a native-speaker linguist, on the Porto-Novo variety; it is not from a phonology section. The phonological descriptions of record (Hazoumé 1979, Feyer 1955, Westermann 1952, Capo 1991) were not opened.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted footnote concerns the Porto-Novo (Benin) variety of Gungbe, i.e. gunn1250 proper. Gbeto 2004 describes Wemɛgbe (Ouémé; Glottolog places Weme under Fon, fonn1241) and only uses Gun-gbe forms as comparanda. Soremekun 1987 concerns Aladagbe (Alada of Nigeria), which Glottolog tags to Gun. Nigerian sources call the language Egun/Ogu/Egungbe.

tone_statements.citation: Gbéto, Flavien. 1998/99. Description et hypothèses sur la nature de l'UPT: l'exemple des langues gbe. Journal of West African Languages 27(2): 3-20.
tone_statements.quote: Les langues gbe sont des langues à tons qui distinguent entre tons ponctuels et tons modulés. ... (1) Exemple de tons ponctuels B: dà préparer (tous les dialectes gbe) H: bé de (dialectes gen) M: nükd oeil (dialectes fon) ... Au niveau lexical, tous les dialectes gbe opposent un ton H à un ton non H. Les tons modulés n'ont pas de statut phonologique (voir Gbéto 1995a, 1997a) et présentent une distribution caractéristique résumée dans les tableaux ci-dessous
tone_statements.translation: The Gbe languages are tone languages that distinguish level tones from contour tones. ... (1) Examples of level tones: L dà 'prepare' (all Gbe dialects), H bé 'of' (Gen dialects), M nukun 'eye' (Fon dialects) ... At the lexical level, all Gbe dialects oppose an H tone to a non-H tone. Contour tones have no phonological status (see Gbéto 1995a, 1997a) and show a characteristic distribution summarised in the tables below.
tone_statements.locator: JWAL 27(2), p. 4, section 2.1 'Tons du gbe' (lect list with 'gun' on pp. 3-4, section 1; Gun informant in fn. 1, p. 3)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: For all Gbe lects incl. Gun: underlying binary opposition H vs non-H; surface level tones L, H and (in the Fon group, to which Gun belongs) M; contour tones LH/HL derived, non-phonemic; author argues the TBU is the segment (vowels and consonants), with consonant voicing conditioning tone realisation; no statement about stress in the pages read.

sources.note: Short pan-Kwa phonology chapter by the volume editors that DOES treat Gungbe tone specifically (Google Books limited-preview snippets, vol. id Eiycx0xz6w8C): p. 1 Kwa languages are tone languages, analysed in the literature with a high vs non-high toneme whose realization is high, low or mid depending on context; p. 2 in Gungbe the high tone is realized high or mid (high when the syllable is nucleus-only, e.g. e with acute), raising the question whether a three-level tonal system should be set up at the tonemic level, plus the Kwa 'key' phenomenon; p. 3 unlike Akan, Gungbe does not seem to us…
